alive.last_commit_message:
A stale client can be a surviving process, not a stale cache (#66)

Everything CLAUDE.md said about a stale client pointed at uv, and none of it
applied to 1.0.17. Both configs read @1.0.17, the 1.0.17 archive was in
uv/cache/archive-v0/, 1.0.17 processes were alive -- and health reported
client_version 1.0.16 across three restarts.

Four processes spawned before the pin was fixed were still running and still
held the session's connection. The app starts new servers without stopping the
old ones, so generations accumulate silently. Killing exactly those four
flipped version_match to true with no further restart.

Only the running process's argv distinguished this from the cache failure
already documented above it, so the Get-CimInstance call goes in as the first
thing to run rather than the last.

The cause of the stale generation is worth its own note:
claude_desktop_config.json is regenerated by the app. An edit there verified as
@1.0.17 and read @1.0.16 again after the next restart, which is the restart
that spawned those four; the same edit to ~/.claude.json held. Both files
define kali-tools and the desktop app reads its own.

Docs only -- no version bump, no rebuild, the pinned gate digest is unaffected.
